preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 10 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 10**5 for n in [int(input().strip()) for _ in range(T)])
preconditions.description: Each test case contains an integer n between 2 and 100,000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(len(permutation) == n for n, permutation in zip([int(input().strip()) for _ in range(T)], [list(map(int, output.split())) for output in stdout.split('\n')]))
postconditions.description: The output permutation for each test case has length n.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= x <= n for x in permutation) for n, permutation in zip([int(input().strip()) for _ in range(T)], [list(map(int, output.split())) for output in stdout.split('\n')]))
postconditions.description: Each element in the output permutation is between 1 and n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(permutation)) == n for n, permutation in zip([int(input().strip()) for _ in range(T)], [list(map(int, output.split())) for output in stdout.split('\n')]))
postconditions.description: Each output permutation contains n distinct elements.

postconditions.expression: all(all(permutation[i] != i + 1 for i in range(n)) for n, permutation in zip([int(input().strip()) for _ in range(T)], [list(map(int, output.split())) for output in stdout.split('\n')]))
postconditions.description: Each output permutation is good, i.e., for any 1 ≤ i ≤ n, pi ≠ i.

postconditions.expression: all(all(permutation[i] < permutation[j] or permutation[i] > permutation[j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n)) for n, permutation in zip([int(input().strip()) for _ in range(T)], [list(map(int, output.split())) for output in stdout.split('\n')]))
postconditions.description: Each output permutation is lexicographically smallest among all good permutations of length n.
